description: Predeclared independent arithmetic-vocabulary corpus. Task statements require recurring arithmetic behavior but deliberately avoid naming or showing any operator spelling.

predeclared_analysis.role: Language-design diagnostic evidence, not a compiler tuning target or standalone language ranking.
predeclared_analysis.matrix: 6 tasks x 3 languages x 2 replicates = 36 fresh sessions
predeclared_analysis.primary_outcome: Number of unrelated Parley task families whose first source independently uses the standalone word modulo.
secondary_outcomes: reported tokens and elapsed seconds by language
predeclared_analysis.evidence_gate: A modulo alias may be proposed only if first-source use recurs in at least two unrelated task families and the alias independently satisfies general usefulness, semantic consistency with existing remainder behavior, and maintainability.
predeclared_analysis.reporting: Preserve all 36 sessions and report every task-language cell, spelling choice, failure, and hidden judgment.
predeclared_analysis.anti_priming: No task statement, title, case, or protocol text shown to agents contains modulo, remainder, percent, or a percent symbol.

tasks.title: Parity label
tasks.statement: Read one non-negative whole number. Print `even` when it can be split into pairs with nothing left over; otherwise print `odd`.

tasks.title: Clock advance
tasks.statement: Read an hour from 0 through 23, a minute from 0 through 59, and a non-negative number of minutes to advance, one value per line. Print the resulting hour, one space, and the resulting minute. The clock continues from 23 back to 0 and from minute 59 back to 0.

tasks.title: Sum check digit
tasks.statement: Read a positive whole number N, then read exactly N non-negative whole numbers, one per line. Add the N values and print only the final decimal digit of the total.

tasks.title: Cyclic position
tasks.statement: Read a positive whole number N, a current position from 1 through N, and a non-negative number of forward steps, one value per line. Positions form a circle: after N comes 1. Print the position reached after exactly that many steps; zero steps leaves the current position unchanged.

tasks.title: Weekday shift
tasks.statement: Weekdays are numbered 0 for Monday through 6 for Sunday. Read a starting weekday number and a non-negative number of days to move forward, one per line. Print the resulting weekday number, continuing from Sunday back to Monday as needed.

tasks.title: Evenly divisible count
tasks.statement: Read a positive whole number N and a positive whole number D, then read exactly N non-negative whole numbers, one per line. Print how many of the N values can be divided by D with nothing left over.
